title: I Took the Letterpress Chase Booking to the Intern Who Left My Furniture

parts.text: I stepped into press one at 10:07 a.m. and intern Jules was already using my numbered furniture. The board said: NINETY MINUTES. FURNITURE STAYS WITH THE CHASE. I was thirty-one, print steward, holding a clipboard that listed our form. Jules shrugged. "Interns learn the bed." I photographed the board, the booking, and his quoins in my chase. Then I asked for the chase booking. At 10:15 the print desk pinged why Jules's quoins sat in our chase. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The print desk can see Jules's quoins in press one during our form.

social.video_title: He left his quoins in my numbered chase — Part 1/2
social.description: Letterpress studio, an intern in my chase, a ninety-minute clock he posted. I logged the quoins. Would you have asked for the chase booking?

parts.text: Jules called it lockup practice until the desk asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the board, and the chase still. The furniture went back to my numbered tray. Jules ran a slot of their own and told the next intern atmosphere was always about optics. Optics is a word people use when a booking exists. Policy now has a second line: INTERNS DO NOT LEARN ON A BOOKED BED. I keep our form on a labeled slate. Jules brown-bags his quoins. The press finally looks like a booking, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Interns do not learn on a booked bed — Part 2/2
social.description: Chase booking, numbered furniture, and a second line on the board. Was lockup ever our form?
